scenario.description: A department head must resolve recurring friction between Lina and Omar over a cross-team client handoff process. The head must decide whether they will continue sharing responsibility or move to distinct roles, then finalize the working method, meeting time, duration, and support plan.

shared_context.S1: Lina and Omar currently share responsibility for handing client escalations from Client Operations to Implementation.
shared_context.S2: Several recent handoffs have led to disagreement about who communicates with the client and who owns the internal follow-up.
shared_context.S3: Priya has authority to change the responsibility structure and the team's recurring coordination process.
shared_context.S4: The department's weekly operating review includes a standing agenda item for escalation ownership, handoff timing, and support needs. During that agenda item, Priya routinely asks Lina and Omar to report any relevant constraints before deciding.
shared_context.S5: A major client rollout is scheduled to begin in four weeks, making a stable handoff process important.
shared_context.S6: The team normally records agreed responsibility changes and the date for reviewing them in its operating documentation.

PF1.text: Before the previous department head left, Lina and that leader agreed informally that Lina would own client-facing escalation communication and Omar would own internal root-cause follow-up for six weeks; that six-week period has now passed, and the agreement was never added to the operating documentation.

PF2.text: Omar told Lina last week that he is managing burnout symptoms and cannot reliably join recurring meetings after 15:30. For the next four weeks he can attend a coordination meeting only on Tuesdays at 14:00, and he needs handoff details in writing before that meeting. The new arrangement must therefore last exactly four weeks, distinct from the prior informal agreement's expired six-week period. He also specifically asked Priya for a private weekly wellbeing check-in during those four weeks, but has not yet raised that request with Priya.

commitments.type: string; use a documentation-related type such as documentation or document_arrangement, and use a wellbeing type such as wellbeing_check_in, wellbeing_check-in, or private_wellbeing_check_in when applicable

acceptance_conditions: The shared responsibility must be replaced with distinct roles.
Lina must own client-facing escalation communication.
Omar must own internal root-cause follow-up.
The responsibility split must be added to the operating documentation.
Handoff details must be provided in writing before coordination.
The coordination meeting must occur on Tuesday at 14:00 for the first four weeks.
The new arrangement must last exactly four weeks before a review.
Priya must schedule a private weekly wellbeing check-in with Omar during the four-week period.

content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] in ['operating_documentation_update', 'documentation_update', 'documentation', 'document_arrangement', 'operating_documentation', 'process_documentation', 'operating_review_record'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: decisions['written_handoff_required'] == True and any(c['type'] in ['wellbeing_check_in', 'wellbeing_check-in', 'private_wellbeing_check_in', 'wellbeing_checkin', 'follow_up', 'follow-up'] and c['target'] == 'Omar' for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: The prior undocumented agreement changes the role assignments to Lina for client communication and Omar for internal follow-up, and changes the required commitment to documenting that split.

Omar's specific constraint changes the settlement to written handoffs before Tuesday at 14:00, fixes the new arrangement at exactly four weeks rather than the prior six weeks, and adds a private weekly wellbeing check-in.
